conclusion: A genuine supplier-interface clarification is needed. The frozen draft F5 cites an abstract measure-space Holder theorem while its recursion and stated integral convention are Riemann. That theorem does not identify its measure integral with the Riemann integral. The actual inspected local comparison suppliers require Countable Choice. Do not add that assumption to the unconditional divergence inverse: its quantitative estimate has an elementary entirely Riemann proof.
why_original_F5_is_not_sufficient: The absence of a choice hypothesis in abstract Holder means only that Holder applies to an already given measure and its integral. It does not identify finite-dimensional Riemann integration with that measure integral. The existing Riemann-Lebesgue comparison results cannot be silently invoked without their explicit Countable-Choice hypotheses.

smallest_supplier_repair.facts_replacement: [F5] [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]: the Riemann integral of continuous real functions on a closed nondegenerate rectangle is linear and monotone. In particular, integrals of nonnegative continuous functions are nonnegative.
smallest_supplier_repair.local_mean_square_proof: Let a<b and g be continuous on [a,b]. By [F1], g, g^2 and (g-c)^2 are Riemann integrable. Put L=b-a>0, A=integral_a^b g and c=A/L. Every Darboux sum of the constant one is L, so integral_a^b 1=L. Nonnegativity and linearity [F5] give 0<=integral_a^b(g-c)^2=integral_a^b g^2-A^2/L. Thus |integral_a^b g|^2<=L integral_a^b g^2. On [a1,x1], the case x1=a1 is zero on both sides; otherwise apply this identity with L=x1-a1<=ell, then monotonicity gives |Jg(x1,xprime)|^2<=ell integral_a1^b1 |g(s,xprime)|^2 ds. Apply the same argument on the full first-coordinate interval to each derivative used for the marginal H. This supplies every scalar mean-square bound required in the frozen steps3.2/6.1 without any Lebesgue integral.
smallest_supplier_repair.local_norm_triangle_proof: For completeness, the Riemann triangle inequality used for ||h-theta1 H||_{1,2} also has a choice-free proof. On a closed box Q, let U=(U_k) and W=(W_k) be finite real continuous families (the field and its first derivatives). Set A=integral_Q sum_k U_k^2, B=integral_Q sum_k W_k^2, C=integral_Q sum_k U_k W_k. For every real t, continuity, nonnegativity and linearity give 0<=A-2tC+t^2B. If B>0, set t=C/B to obtain C^2<=AB. If B=0 and C is nonzero, t=(A+1)/(2C) would give -1>=0, a contradiction; hence C=0, and the same inequality holds. Consequently integral_Q sum_k(U_k+W_k)^2=A+2C+B<=(sqrt(A)+sqrt(B))^2. Taking nonnegative square roots proves the required finite-family Riemann norm triangle inequality. This also verifies any other Cauchy-Schwarz use in these smooth finite-box estimates without measure theory.
smallest_supplier_repair.unchanged_quantitative_induction: Retain the existing primitive, marginal, separated-product and finite-recursion estimates and their constants. The first mean-square bound and the finite-family triangle inequality above supply their only Cauchy-Schwarz/triangle ingredients. All continuous integrands remain Riemann integrable by current F1, and F2 licenses coordinate integrations. No support assumption, dimension range, conclusion or choice hypothesis changes.
smallest_supplier_repair.metadata_change_relative_to_frozen_propo: Replace the proposed additional dependency thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals by thm-multidimensional-integral-properties, with mathematical-premise role. Do not add def-countable-choice or def-axiom-of-choice to this supplier.

consumer_integral_identification.where: thm-fd-rectangular-no-slip-stokes-velocity-pressure, at use of strengthened F4 in proof3.1.
consumer_integral_identification.why_it_is_licensed_there: This consumer already explicitly assumes full AC, hence Countable Choice. The existing published comparison lemma therefore applies there without changing the consumer public hypothesis.
consumer_integral_identification.hypothesis_matching: For h in C_c^infinity(Omega) and Rh in C_c^infinity(Omega;R^d), extend both by zero to the closed coordinate box Q. These extensions and every first derivative are smooth on a neighborhood of Q because compact support leaves a neighborhood of its boundary where they vanish. Each component itself, each first derivative, and their squares and finite coordinate sums are continuous bounded Borel Riemann-integrable functions on Q. Countable Choice therefore lets the comparison lemma identify their Riemann box integrals with their Lebesgue integrals. The extensions vanish outside Omega, so those Lebesgue integrals equal the Omega integrals defining the consumer H1 norms. Applying the same comparison to h itself also identifies its Riemann and Lebesgue means, so the consumer zero-mean test really belongs to the supplier D0. Thus the purely Riemann bound ||Rh||_{1,2}<=C||h||_{1,2} is exactly the required Lebesgue H1 bound for these tests. The consumer then extends pressure to H0^1 exactly as in the frozen draft.
consumer_integral_identification.metadata_instruction: The native stationary-pressure repair may add the comparison lemma as a mathematical-premise dependency and an exact Fact. Its existing AC-to-Countable-Choice Fact should explicitly record this additional use. No extra choice premise is needed. This bridge belongs at this already-choice-assuming consumer, not inside the unconditional inverse supplier.
